stem: A 16-year-old boy has had 3 days of sharp left chest pain that lasts seconds and is worse when he twists. He is afebrile. Pressing over the left fourth costochondral junction reproduces the pain. Heart, lungs and ECG are normal.

ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.B: Pericarditis gives a **rub and diffuse ST elevation**; his ECG and heart exam are normal

set_title: High lactate with weak muscles, stroke-like spells or brainstem signs: which mitochondrial or energy defect
stem: A 21-year-old woman has painful muscle cramps and dark urine after lifting weights. If she rests for a few minutes, she can resume without pain.
oneliner: 21F + cramps and dark urine after lifting weights + pain-free again after a short rest → ?
ask: What is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.B: Leigh syndrome is an infantile brain disease; she is **21 with exertional cramps and dark urine**
whyNot.C: MELAS causes headaches and stroke-like episodes; she has **exertional cramps with dark urine and relief by rest**
whyNot.D: Pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency presents in infancy; she is **21 with exertional cramps and pigmenturia**
whyNot.E: Mitochondrial myopathy causes slowly progressive weakness and early fatigue; she has **cramps with dark urine that ease after a short rest**

set_title: One hot swollen joint: crystals, infection or wear
stem: A 55-year-old man who drinks beer heavily wakes at night with an exquisitely painful, red, swollen first metatarsophalangeal joint. Chalky nodules are present on his fingers and ear.
oneliner: 55M + heavy beer + night-time red painful big toe + chalky nodules on fingers and ear → ?
ask: What is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.A: Pseudogout is an older adult's knee or wrist arthritis with cartilage calcification; he has **a first-toe attack with chalky tophi**
whyNot.B: Septic arthritis does not produce chalky nodules; he has **tophi on the fingers and ear**
whyNot.C: Osteoarthritis causes use-related pain without acute redness or nodules of deposited crystal; he has **an acutely red joint with chalky tophi**
whyNot.D: A ruptured Baker cyst swells the calf behind the knee; he has **a red first metatarsophalangeal joint**

why: Alcohol raises urate production and lowers its renal excretion, so monosodium urate precipitates in the joint and soft tissue. **An acute night-time attack of the first toe with chalky tophi** is gout. Joint fluid shows needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals.

stem: A 68-year-old woman has lost 4 cm in height over 10 years and has a new vertebral compression fracture after lifting a laundry basket. Serum calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase and PTH are normal, and serum protein electrophoresis shows no abnormal band.

set_title: Weak or cramping muscles: a missing protein, a missing enzyme, a potassium shift or disuse
stem: A 4-year-old boy has trouble climbing stairs and pushes on his thighs with his hands to stand up. His calves are large and firm.
oneliner: 4M + trouble with stairs, pushes on thighs to stand + large firm calves → ?
ask: What is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.A: Limb-girdle dystrophy begins in adolescence or adulthood with girdle weakness in either sex; this patient is a **4-year-old boy with large, firm calves**
whyNot.C: Pompe disease presents with a floppy infant, a large tongue and an enlarged heart; this child has **large firm calves and pushes on his thighs to stand**
whyNot.D: Hypokalemic periodic paralysis gives attacks of weakness that clear between episodes; he has **steady trouble with stairs and needs his hands to stand**
whyNot.E: McArdle disease causes cramps with exercise and normal strength at rest; this boy has **constant proximal weakness with enlarged calves**

ask: Which single finding best favors axillary nerve injury over radial nerve injury?

options.A: Numbness over the skin of the lateral shoulder
options.B: Wrist drop with weak extension of the fingers
options.C: Swelling and bruising over the upper arm
options.D: Tenderness over the fracture site on palpation
options.E: Loss of sensation over the dorsum of the first web space

whyNot.B: Wrist drop marks radial nerve injury, the other candidate, and **points away from axillary injury**

set_title: Child or teen with knee pain or a limp: the knee itself or the hip
stem: A 13-year-old boy who plays soccer has had 3 weeks of right knee pain that is worse with running and jumping. The tibial tubercle is swollen and tender, and hip motion is normal.
